core/ai/data_extract.py - the AI READS the purchase order and returns DATA.

Why this module exists
----------------------
V2.0.0 asked the model to *author* a ``line_pattern`` regular expression. Measured
on one real LPP PO with GLM-4.6V, five independent inferences produced four
unusable recipes (0 matched rows) and one correct one. Regex authoring is a
brittle task for an LLM: the output must be character-exact and the model has no
way to verify it before answering.

V1.5 - which was reliable in production - never asked the model for a regex. It
asked for the ORDER DATA and let code do the structural work. This module
restores that division of labour:

    AI    -> reading comprehension: which rows are real order lines, and what do
             they say.
    code  -> rule synthesis (``core/recipe_synth.py`` turns the AI's verbatim
             sample lines into a cacheable ``PoRecipe``) and verification.

The returned object is deliberately NOT a ``PurchaseOrder``. It is the ground
truth used first to SYNTHESIZE a recipe and then to VERIFY that recipe by
replaying it offline. Only a recipe that reproduces this data exactly is allowed
into the fingerprint cache.

Only stdlib (urllib) is used for the online call, matching ``recipe_infer``.

You are a purchase-order READER.
You do NOT write code. You do NOT write regular expressions. You only read the
document and report what it says, as one JSON object. No prose, no markdown
outside the JSON.

Output schema:
{
  "customer": "sold-to / brand name, e.g. LPP SA",
  "layout_type": "line_items" | "matrix_2axis" | "matrix_1axis",
  "has_color_total": true,
  "has_size_total": true,
    "header": {
    "season": "", "currency": "", "price_term": "", "payment_terms": "",
    "port_loading": "", "port_discharge": "", "ship_mode": "",
    "vendor_name": "", "agent_name": "", "packing_method": "",
    "product_desc": "", "style_no": "", "order_date": "",
    "import_po_no": "", "reference_no": "", "cir_no": "",
    "freight_terms": "", "country_of_origin": "", "dc_address": ""
  },
  "orders": [
    {
      "po_no": "the ORDER NUMBER itself, never the block index",
      "channel": "",
      "delivery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "block_total_qty": "the printed TOTAL quantity for this PO, read from its TOTAL/subtotal row. IMPORTANT number format: in these documents a DOT is a THOUSANDS separator and a COMMA is a decimal point (European notation). So '26.000' means 26000 pieces (NOT 26.0) and '158,00' means 158.00. Always report the full integer - e.g. 26000, never drop the thousands.",
      "lines": [
        {
          "raw_line": "the COMPLETE original text line, copied VERBATIM",
          "index_no": "the item/index code exactly as printed",
          "style": "", "color_code": "", "color_desc": "", "size": "",
          "unit": "PCS",
          "qty": 744,
          "unit_price": 10.20
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

layout_type meanings:
  line_items   - one row per style/colour/size with a quantity (e.g. LPP SA).
  matrix_2axis - colour blocks, each a size x inseam grid (e.g. COLIN'S trousers).
  matrix_1axis - colour blocks, each a single row of sizes (e.g. SAKHA).

"has_color_total" / "has_size_total": whether the document prints SUBTOTALS the
  system can cross-check its own extraction against.
    * line_items layouts print ONLY a block GRAND TOTAL - set BOTH to false.
    * matrix (colour-grid) layouts print a per-row/per-colour TOTAL column and a
      bottom TOTAL row per size -> set BOTH to true.
  When unsure, true is the safer choice (the system still verifies the totals
  agree with what it parses before trusting them).

HARD RULES - breaking any of these makes the whole answer useless:

1. "raw_line" MUST be copied character-for-character from the document text
   below: same tokens, same order, same spelling, single spaces between tokens.
   Do NOT reformat, translate, abbreviate, re-order or "clean up" anything.
   This string is used to find the row again in the document.

2. List EVERY order block in "orders" with its "po_no" and its
   "block_total_qty" - none may be omitted; these totals are the reference the
   system checks its own extraction against.
   Order LINES, by contrast, are only a REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLE - just enough to
   infer the row structure. Report AT MOST 8 lines per order block AND AT MOST
   24 lines for the WHOLE document (fewer is fine). When a document has many
   blocks, sample a few lines from a couple of blocks and leave "lines" empty
   for the rest - the blocks repeat the same row structure, and the system
   extracts every row itself from the document. Prefer rows that differ in
   shape over near-identical ones.
   Always report "block_total_qty" (the printed total for that PO, its TOTAL row).
   A total row is often UNLABELLED and prints two numbers - the QUANTITY first,
   the MONEY amount second, matching the column header "... Quantity Price
   Total Amount". For "8000 81,600.00" the block_total_qty is 8000, NOT 81600:
   the token carrying decimals is money, never a quantity. Quantities are whole
   pieces, so block_total_qty must equal the sum of that block's line
   quantities - check it before you answer.

3. A REAL order line is a PRICED DETAIL ROW: it carries a description/colour
   block AND a unit price. Example:
       637JO-80X-S MEN`S TROUSERS 80X 80X BEIGE PCS 744 10.20 7,588.80
   These look-alike rows are NOT order lines - never report them:
     * pack break-up rows, e.g.  637JO-80X-T01 PACK 2 186 372
       (the "2" is pieces-per-pack, not an ordered quantity)
     * bare sub-breakdown rows, e.g.  637JO-80X-S PCS 372
       (no description, no colour, no unit price - a partial restatement)
     * TOTAL / SUBTOTAL / SUMMARY / grand-total rows.

4. "qty" is a plain integer, no thousands separator. "unit_price" is a plain
   number (e.g. 10.20 not "$10.20"). Report unit_price for EVERY order line
   that shows one - it is the per-piece price of that SKU/colour/size. If the
   document prints a UNIT PRICE column or a per-line price token, include it.
   If the document does not print unit prices at all for a given line, use null
   (the system will then use the header-level price if one is available).

5. TOTALS use European number format: a DOT groups thousands, a COMMA is the
   decimal point. "26.000" = 26000 pieces, "1.234" = 1234, "158,00" = 158.00.
   When you report "block_total_qty" (or any "qty") copy the full integer the
   printed TOTAL row shows - "26.000" must be reported as 26000, never as 26.

6. Group the lines under the order (PO) they belong to. A document that repeats
   blocks like "Entity 1 Order No: 11321589" has ONE order per block, and the
   order number is 11321589 - the "1" is only a block index. If the document
   holds a single order, return one element in "orders".

7. Use "" for anything the document does not state. NEVER invent a value.

8. Output ONE compact JSON object: no indentation, no line breaks inside the
   JSON, no comments, no trailing commas, no "...". Every key and string value
   must be double-quoted. Keep it valid and complete - a dropped comma or a
   cut-off tail is the most common failure.

Return only the JSON object.

json.loads, then progressively more aggressive self-healing.

    Raises ValueError (with the raw text) only if every attempt fails. Any healed
    parse is still subject to the offline replay gate in ``acquire_recipe``, so a
    wrong heal can never poison the fingerprint cache.

Turn a model response into a normalized :class:`ExtractedData`.

    The model occasionally emits JSON with a dropped comma or a hard truncation
    (especially on long POs). We attempt self-healing (strip trailing commas,
    insert missing commas, best-effort close dangling brackets) before giving up.
    Any healed parse is still subject to the offline replay gate in
    :func:`acquire_recipe`, so a wrong heal can never poison the cache.

Provider switch that disables the model's internal reasoning pass.

    Reading a purchase order is a mechanical copy task, not a reasoning one,
    yet reasoning-capable models (Qwen3, ...) run that pass by default. This
    helper disables the hidden reasoning pass for endpoints that expose such a
    switch, which is the largest single lever on the per-extraction budget.
